To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal sensitivity of a Michelson interferometer with two Doppler readouts is equal to $\approx 2.5$ times that of a Michelson with only a single Doppler readout, that the optimal sensitivity is achieved by combining three interferometers, and that the sensitivity improvement over the single interferometer is approximately $\sqrt{2.5} \approx 1.58$.

the optimal sensitivity of LISA can be achieved with the following three interferometric combinations: (1) the Michelson combination, (2) the sum of two Doppler combinations, and (3) the difference of two Doppler combination.

LISA's sensitivity to sinusoidal sources is improved by a factor of $\sqrt{2+4\sin^2\pi f\tau}$ over a single Michleson interferometer, where $f$ is the gravitational wave frequency in Hz and $\tau$ is the one-way light-travel time in the LISA arms in seconds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of the sensitivity of the LISA space-based gravitational wave antenna.
the optimal combination of the interferometric combinations available on LISA.
the optimal use of the multiple Doppler measurements available in the LISA mission, and the results of this research are expected to improve the LISA sensitivity to gravitational waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensitivity improvement over the Michleson combination is always greater than $\sqrt 3$ in the frequency band of interest.
the LISA sensitivity to sinusoidal gravitational waves is improved by a factor $\sim \sqrt{\pi/2} \sim 1.25$ over that of the single Michelson combination.

, in the nominal LISA configuration, a triplet of interferometers with optimal combination can improve the sensitivity of LISA over the Michelson combination by a factor of about $\sqrt{2.5}$, with the improvement being greatest at the high end of the LISA band.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for sinusoidal gravitational waves in the LISA frequency band, the LISA optimal combination has a sensitivity gain of $\sqrt{3}$.
LISA will be sensitive to a larger number of sources than a single Michelson combination, with a broadened frequency band, and with an average sensitivity gain of 1.3.

the optimal combination of LISA interferometers is a triplet of observables with the same sensitivity as three independent Michelson combinations, but with a broader band of best sensitivity and with a sensitivity that is greater than the sensitivity of a single Michelson combination at all frequencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LISA interferometric combinations are not all equivalent in their sensitivity.
, by judiciously combining the Doppler readouts, the sensitivity of the LISA mission can be improved over that of a single Michelson combination.
LISA will be capable of forming interferometric combinations that are optimal in the sense of maximizing the sensitivity to gravitational waves and minimizing the sensitivity to instrumental noises.
